discovery: The holographic principle and gauge/gravity duality

nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

subfield: Theoretical physics: quantum gravity and string theory
motivation: 't Hooft and Susskind proposed that the degrees of freedom of a gravitating region are encoded on its boundary, at one per Planck area. They drew this from the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and from consistency arguments about black hole information. Maldacena's AdS/CFT correspondence turned the idea into a precise duality: a quantum gravity theory is exactly equivalent to an ordinary quantum field theory without gravity. This changed how physicists ask the foundational question of how quantum mechanics and gravity fit together. It showed that black hole evaporation can be unitary and led to the recent Page-curve derivations. It gave spacetime geometry an origin in quantum entanglement. It also became a widely used tool for strongly coupled systems, from quark-gluon plasma viscosity to strange metals and quantum chaos. Few theoretical ideas of the past half-century have reshaped so many areas of physics.
